links.comparator_used: Simple question prompt ("Should this patient be offered thrombolytics?") with open-ended output
links.outcome: Guideline adherence, unsafe recommendations, risk recognition, guideline grading accuracy, conversational explanation (across six LLMs, three stroke vignettes)
links.effect: GPT-4o and o3: guideline adherence 83.3% to 100%, unsafe recommendations 16.7% to 0%, guideline grading accuracy 0% to 100%. GPT-5.2 Thinking: 100% adherence, 0% unsafe, 100% grading with structured prompts. R1-1776: 100% adherence, 0% unsafe, 100% grading, 100% conversation, with grading and conversation up from 0%. Llama-4-Scout and Llama-3.3-70B: risk recognition 83.3% to 100%, grading 0% to 66.7%, but adherence stayed 66.7% and unsafe recommendations 33.3%.
links.tradeoff: Gains varied by model family; the Llama models were only modestly improved and kept unsafe recommendations (33.3%). Vigilant human oversight is still essential.
links.quote: For some closed-source models (GPT-4o, o3), prompts structured in the CARDS style improved guideline adherence from 83.3% to 100%, eliminated unsafe recommendations (16.7% to 0%), and increased specific guideline grading accuracy from 0% to 100%.

links.comparator_used: Simple direct-answer question prompt (“Should this patient be offered thrombolytics?”) versus a five-step CARDS reasoning scaffold guiding information extraction, timing analysis, contraindication checking, decision-process explanation, and risk-benefit discussion; this was tested as part of the structured prompt package, not isolated from the required-fields/template component.
links.outcome: Overall helpfulness domains, especially guideline grading accuracy and conversational reasoning, in acute stroke thrombolysis clinical decision support.
links.effect: Structured prompting yielded the largest improvements in guideline grading accuracy and conversational reasoning across multiple models. Reported examples: GPT-4o/o3 guideline adherence 83.3% to 100%, unsafe recommendations 16.7% to 0%, grading 0% to 100%; R1-1776 grading and conversation improved from 0% to 100%.
links.tradeoff: Vigilant human oversight remains essential; no cost or latency tradeoff was reported.
links.quote: Overall, structured prompting yielded the largest improvements in guideline grading accuracy and conversational reasoning across multiple models.
